items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: They had a trumpet player from Buffalo that joined the band, named Frank Beard or something like that.

ctx.x: So, he never rang it while you soloed.

No, (laughs) never did. In fact, I played two, three solos and played on mute one night and that’s where the name Sweets came from. He nicknamed me Sweets. He called me Sweetie Pie, then cut the Pie off and from then on, it was the name Sweets. And Basie was such a funny guy—I’m speaking of him because that’s the only band that I ever knew, was the Count Basie band. They had a trumpet player from Buffalo that joined the band, named Frank Beard or something like that. Every piece he would jump up and take a solo,…
Who in the band was helpful to you when you first joined, did anyone try and show you the ropes since you had no written arrangements, did anyone try and cue you in as to…
